newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's Jagland appointed new prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Jagland appointed new prime minister.

text.p: Thorbjoern Jagland was appointed prime minister of Norway on Friday, succeeding political veteran Gro Harlem Brundtland, an official statement said.
It said King Harald V appointed Jagland and his Labour minority government as of 12.30 p.m. (1030gmt) after accepting the resignation of Brundtland and her 18-member cabinet.
The statement said the new government's distribution of ministeries would be formally decided during a special session of the Council of State in the Royal Palace.

The statement however confirmed press reports that Industry and Energy Minister Jens Stoltenberg was succeeding Sigbjoern Johnsen as finance minister. Stoltenberg will hand over his portfolio to Justice Minister Grete Faremo, it said.

Brundtland, 57, who dominated Norwegian politics for 15 years and was in office for 10 years, said in a surprise announcement on Wednesday that she was resigning to give the ruling Labour party a fresh start for next year's elections.
Jagland, who as party leader has been groomed four years to become premier, has said there will be no change in Norway's policies.
